name: Lies, Lies, Lies
topic: really weird hiding places for money

items.name: Al Capone's empty vault
items.fact: In 1986, a TV reporter opened a secret vault under a Chicago hotel once used by the gangster Al Capone, live on TV, in front of millions of viewers. He found only dirt and some empty bottles.

items.name: Gold in the piano
items.fact: In 2016, a piano tuner in Shropshire, England, opened an old piano that had been given to a local college and found 913 gold coins hidden inside it. Nobody knows who put them there.

items.name: Coins in tin cans
items.fact: In 2013, a couple walking their dog on their land in California found rusty tin cans full of gold coins from the 1800s, worth about $10 million. It is one of the largest finds in US history.

items.name: The money in the sofa
items.fact: In 2014, three students in New York State bought an old sofa for $20 from a charity shop and found $40,800 in cash hidden inside it. They returned the money to the elderly woman who had hidden it.

items.name: The million in the mattress
items.fact: In 2009, a woman in Tel Aviv bought her elderly mother a new mattress as a surprise and threw out the old one. Inside it were her mother's life savings, about $1 million. It was never found.

items.name: The cold cash
items.fact: In 2005, FBI agents searching the home of a US congressman found $90,000 in cash in his freezer, wrapped in foil and hidden in food boxes. He was later sent to prison for bribery.

items.name: Money in the walls
items.fact: In 2006, a builder renovating an old house in Cleveland, Ohio, found about $182,000 in cash from the 1920s and 1930s hidden in the walls. The builder and the owner then fought over it in court.

items.name: Money for rats
items.fact: According to Pablo Escobar's brother, the drug gang had so much cash hidden in walls and fields that it spent $2,500 a month on rubber bands, and rats ate part of the money every year.

items.name: Wedding savings eaten by termites
items.fact: In 2023, a woman in northern India opened her bank safe-deposit box and found that termites had eaten the cash she had saved there for her daughter's wedding, about 1.8 million rupees.

items.name: The treasure in the mountains
items.fact: In 2010, Forrest Fenn, an American art dealer, hid a bronze chest full of gold and jewels somewhere in the Rocky Mountains and published a poem with clues. Ten years later, someone finally found it.

fakes.name: The bread-oven savings
fakes.fact: In 2018, a Polish baker found €12,000 in old banknotes rolled up inside a broken bread oven he had bought from a closed bakery. The previous owner had hidden them during the war.

fakes.name: Notes in the hymn books
fakes.fact: A church in rural Austria found 40,000 schillings in banknotes hidden between the pages of old hymn books in 2011. The money was out of date and was given to a museum.

fakes.name: The garden gnome bank
fakes.fact: In 2015, a German pensioner told the police that thieves had taken the garden gnome where she kept her savings. They returned the gnome, but not the €8,000 inside.

fakes.name: Cash in the cheese
fakes.fact: Customs officers at a Swiss border crossing found €50,000 inside three large hollowed-out wheels of cheese in 2017. The driver said he did not know it was there.

fakes.name: Coins in the chimney
fakes.fact: A chimney sweep in Yorkshire found 300 silver coins from the 1800s inside a chimney in 2019. They had been hidden in a leather bag on a ledge.

fakes.name: Savings in the fish tank
fakes.fact: A man in Lisbon hid his savings in a waterproof box under the gravel of his fish tank. In 2016 his son sold the tank online, box and all.

fakes.name: Money in the guitar
fakes.fact: In 2020, a music shop in Madrid bought an old Spanish guitar and found €7,500 in banknotes taped inside it. The money was returned to the late owner's family.

fakes.name: The lost key in the lake
fakes.fact: A Finnish businessman threw the key to his safe into a lake in 2012 after an argument with his business partner. Divers spent two weeks looking for it.

fakes.name: The bank in a beehive
fakes.fact: A beekeeper in Slovenia kept his savings inside an empty beehive for twenty years. He said that no thief would want to put a hand inside.

fakes.name: Banknotes in the ceiling
fakes.fact: Builders renovating a primary school in Belgium in 2018 found 60,000 francs hidden above the ceiling of the head teacher's office. The francs were no longer worth anything.

fake: Give it a short, newspaper-style name.
Something weird but possible: a piece of furniture, a building, an animal, a place outside.
A person, a family or a business, and a real town or country.
Who found it, and how: a builder, a buyer, the police, by accident.
Who got the money, or what went wrong.
A number, a date or a small strange detail.
tips: Be specific: numbers, dates and real places make a lie believable.
Give it a small problem (“the notes were no longer worth anything”): perfect things sound fake.
Make both talks the same length and give them the same confidence.
Don't laugh. Decide now who says which one.
